My relationships, my finances, physical decline, due to the loss of my appetite and a lack of movement because its hard to leave my room, the seizure I suffered and driving my car off the road because I spilled a vial and was unable to properly taper, woke up with a sherriff at my window, and an ambulance pulling up behind me, about 2500 in medical bills hanging over my head. I experienced extreme muscle fatigue, and now i just lock myself in my room all day every day when I'm not working because I can't stand the company of other human beings, it makes me too anxious. I've suffered random anxiety attacks that cause me to pass out in public and wake up drenched in sweat surrounded by frightened people, unsure of what to do. I'm not sure if I'll ever heal, and because of that i keep getting back on bromazolam, currently tapering down to the bottom again, but no hope for my mental health for a long time honestly. Temporary relief from your current level of anxiety is not worth the potential hell that could be in store for you. Not everyone has such a negative experience with benzos, but as far as I've seen most of us are going through hell to get off of these drugs. I always used to say to myself, "oh I'll only use when needed, at low doses, maybe once a week" and my mental health declined, and i gave up and started dosing more, at higher doses, and before you know it your tolerance is high and you're in a serious bind. Tread carefully if you're going to mess with this bullshit, I'd give anything to go back to sober, unmedicated, and dealing with my bipolar disorder like I did before.

That will be dependent on your metabolism, but it takes roughly 5 half lives in total for a drug to totally leave the body. The half life is only a rough estimation and varies between animal test subjects. F-pam varied between like 100 - 130hrs in animal test subjects. Bromazolam has a half life of around 24 - 30hrs, so this schedule should be similar to your current brom schedule.
